subject: Your bank is not calling you
preheader: A phone scam to hang up on, a screenshot shortcut, and AI that explains letters.
intro: Three short things this week. The first one could save you real money.

sections.label: Scam of the week
sections.title: The "bank fraud department" phone call
paragraphs: Someone calls saying they're from your bank's fraud department. They sound serious. They say your account is in danger and you must act right now: move money, read out a code, or install something.
bullets: Hang up. A real bank won't mind.
Call the number printed on the back of your card or on your bank's website, not a number the caller gave you and not the number on your caller ID.
Never read out a code that was texted to you. That code is the key to your account.

sections.label: Tip of the week
sections.title: Take a screenshot
paragraphs: A screenshot is a photo of your screen. It's handy for saving a confirmation, a map, or an error message to show someone.
bullets: iPhone with Face ID: press the side button and the volume-up button together, then let go.
Most Android phones: press the power button and the volume-down button together.
Find the picture afterward in your Photos or Gallery app.
sections.note: The buttons differ a little by model. If it doesn't work, search "screenshot" plus your phone's name.

sections.label: AI trick of the week
sections.title: Explain that letter in plain English
paragraphs: Got a confusing notice? Type or paste the words in and ask AI to explain them.
sections.prompt: Explain this in plain English, as if I've never seen it before, and tell me what I need to do and by when: [paste the text here]
sections.note: Remove your name, address and account numbers before you paste anything, and check anything important with the sender.
